RINs are generated when designated biofuels are imported or produced and conveyed with the volumetric sale of those biofuels until blended with petroleum products or sold to an obligated party. Source: EPA (2025e, 2025f) The 2022 Inflation Reduction Act created the 45Z credit to encourage domestic biofuels production. The 2025 credit available to American-controlled biofuels producers was $1.75/gal for SAF and $1.00/gal for other biofuels meeting various criteria. 45Z was amended in the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act providing clarification on allowable feedstocks from the United States, Canada, and Mexico, and the credit is up to $1.00 for biofuels meeting criteria for biofuels produced between Jan. 1, 2026, through Dec. 31, 2029. There are several other programs that enable biofuels, including loan guarantee programs from both the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) and U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA). The Alternative Fuel Infrastructure Tax Credit provides a tax credit of 30% of infrastructure costs or 6% of property subject to deprecation up to $100,000 expiring Dec. 31, 2032. (IRS 2023). In recent years, USDA has provided grants to gas station and terminals owners to extend the availability of ethanol and biodiesel under the Higher Blends Infrastructure Incentive Program (USDA 2025). 2.2 Feedstocks In 2024, 98% of domestic ethanol production was from corn grain, 1% from cellulosic biomass, 1% from sorghum and wheat, and less than 1% from waste sugars (RFA 2024). The 1% cellulosic biomass is derived entirely from bolt-on technology at existing conventional ethanol plants that extracts the nonedible corn kernel fiber, which is designated as a cellulosic feedstock under the RFS. In 2024, 36% of U.S. corn production was used to produce ethanol (USDA Economic Research Service 2025).
